html:
The Act of Free Choice was the vote in 1969 by which western New Guinea became part of Indonesia. Instead of a vote by all, 1,025 chosen representatives voted unanimously to join Indonesia.

The Dutch had kept the territory after the revolution, but handed it over through the United Nations in 1963 under American pressure. The UN accepted the result, though many observers called it a sham.

A Papuan independence movement has fought on ever since. Migration from other islands, partly under transmigration, and the huge Grasberg gold and copper mine have deepened the conflict. See Western New Guinea.
